stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M in Series C
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. The investment highlights the increasing demand for co-orbital security and space domain awareness solutions, particularly from the DoD. Their focus on security in space is a timely response to rising geopolitical tensions.
stories.soWhat: In a world where satellites are becoming the new battlegrounds, True Anomaly's cash influx suggests investors are betting on the inevitability of space conflict.

stories.head: SpaceX finally deploys satellites on 13th test flight
stories.body: SpaceX successfully launched Starship on its 13th test flight, deploying functioning satellites for the first time. After a series of explosive mishaps, this flight is a much-needed win for the company and its ambitious plans for future missions. The test flight indicates a possible return to operational normalcy for SpaceX's flagship vehicle.
stories.soWhat: With Starship now functioning as intended, the clock is ticking for competitors to catch up—especially those still grounded by financial woes.

stories.head: Palantir wins $480M extension for TITAN program
stories.body: Palantir Technologies secured a $480 million contract extension for its TITAN ground station program, reinforcing its position in the defense sector. This funding emphasizes the growing reliance on advanced data analytics in military operations, as the DoD seeks to enhance its situational awareness capabilities. Palantir's ability to secure large contracts continues to validate its business model.
stories.soWhat: Palantir's success in the defense arena suggests that government contracts are less about innovation and more about proven reliability—an interesting play in an industry often obsessed with the next big thing.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
